text:
Maya Patel: Proposal — add a 'stale zone reads' routing policy to let the gateway serve slightly stale cached responses from the local zone when cross-zone write/primary reads exceed a latency cutoff. Goal: reduce P99 tail for read-heavy routes in multi-zone setups. :thinking:

Frank Lin: Could be useful. Main concerns: correctness (staleness window), per-route opt-in, and how we signal downstream services. I think it should be explicit via header/route config, not global.

Liam O'Connor: Agreed. Suggest a latency cutoff param (e.g., `latency_cutoff_ms = 120`) and a `max_staleness_s = 30`. If observed latency to primary > cutoff, route switches to local cached replica for up to max_staleness.

Sarah Gómez: Rollout/UX note: expose this in Console as a toggle on each route with a small canary (5% traffic) and a kitchen-sink view in the Route Details page showing stale-read rate and staleness distribution. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Frank Lin: Implementation detail: gateway should insert `x-redwood-stale-ok: true` header to downstream replicas and set `x-redwood-origin-zone` for observability. Also we need a route matcher rule to opt-in. Example config: 

```
route:
  match: "/v1/search/*"
  policy:
    type: stale_zone_read
    latency_cutoff_ms: 120
    max_staleness_s: 30
    header_override:
      prefer_zone_header: "x-redwood-prefer-zone"
      set_on_forward: { "x-redwood-stale-ok": "true" }
```

Liam O'Connor: Telemetry we should emit: `route.stale_reads.count`, `route.stale_reads.staleness_ms.hist`, `route.stale_reads.fallback_zone.count`, and a tag for `origin_zone`. That lets us build the Console panels and SLO burn alerts.

Maya Patel: Quotas/billing question — do we charge stale reads at the same unit-cost? If they're cheaper to serve (local cache), we could show a separate cost line item. Thoughts?

Frank Lin: I'd prefer to keep billing the same for now to avoid complexity. But add metric `route.stale_reads.cost_estimate` so finance can analyze.

Liam O'Connor: Also consider network egress quotas per-region; stale-reads will reduce cross-zone egress which is good, but we should track `egress_bytes.saved_by_stale_reads`.

Sarah Gómez: Rollout plan in Console: 1) feature flag + UI toggle, 2) 5% canary, 3) 100% if metrics OK. Expose a one-click rollback and an automated SLO guard that disables stale reads if error_rate > 0.5% or staleness > configured max.

Frank Lin: Edge cases: write-after-read hazards. We should only enable stale reads for idempotent GET-like routes or explicitly annotated responses (cacheable by origin). Gateway must respect `cache-control` and route metadata.

Liam O'Connor: For diagnostics add header `x-redwood-stale-used: zone-a;staleness=12s` so apps and logs can correlate. Also recommend a trace tag `redwood.stale_read=true`.

Sarah Gómez: UX: Console should show a diff view of example responses (fresh vs stale) for customers to inspect risk. Add a checkbox "allow up to N seconds stale" in UI.

deploy-bot: Canary job started for `stale_zone_read` policy on service `search-api` — canary=5% -> instances: zone-a(2), zone-b(2). Logs: `deploy:stale_policy:canary:ok`

Maya Patel: Next steps: 1) Frank to sketch gateway PR + header/schema, 2) Liam to add telemetry + tracing proposal, 3) Sarah to mock Console toggle and canary UX, 4) small experiment on one customer route. I'll create the RFC doc this afternoon. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
